_note: Adding a population estimate is a data commit, not a code change: run app/etl/masque_population_etl.R, commit the JSON it writes into this folder, and add its path here. app/population.html validates each listed file against app/etl/population_estimates.schema.json before rendering it and refuses anything that fails. Paths are relative to app/. One artifact per survey cycle (plus an age-restricted comparator where noted); cycles and surveys are not pooled.

reviewed.reason: No headache item: the NHIS pain module, which carries PAIHDFC3M_A, is fielded in odd years only. The phenotype requires the headache arm, so no estimate is possible for this year.
reviewed.wouldChange: Nothing in this file; use the adjacent odd-year cycles.

reviewed.reason: The extract (445,200 adults, 72 of the survey's columns) keeps the weight _LLCPWT but drops the stratum _STSTR and PSU _PSU, so no design-based interval can be computed. BRFSS 2022 also has no headache, dizziness or tinnitus item; the only ear item is DEAF (serious difficulty hearing). The extract codes 'not asked' as 0 (DEAF = 0 for 18,644 adults), which would read as a negative answer.
reviewed.wouldChange: The full LLCP2022 file would restore the design and the blanks, but still could not express the phenotype: it would support a hearing-difficulty component estimate only.

reviewed.reason: In every single year fewer than 30 sample visits carry the phenotype (headache plus dizziness, hearing or tinnitus diagnosis at one visit: 28, 30, 5 and 6 visits of all ages) or the sinusitis-with-headache overlap (31, 10, 8 and 11), so single-year estimates fail the NCHS standard. The four years are pooled instead, as NCHS recommends for rare conditions; the pooled estimates are listed above. 2017 is absent: no codebook was available for that year when the files were collected (reported by the project lead).
reviewed.wouldChange: NAMCS 2017 and later years, which would add sample visits to the pool.

reviewed.reason: Proposal 7.2 benchmarks the MASQUE extractor on FAERS case narratives. In the original openFDA JSON (53,990 records), only 24 records carry the narrative field (patient.summary.narrativeincludeclinical), and every one holds only a 'CASE EVENT DATE' stamp; no record has clinical text. As a partial check, the extractor was run on the MedDRA terms themselves: it recognises headache terms and TINNITUS, but not plain MIGRAINE, not DIZZINESS or VERTIGO without a duration (by design), not any hearing-loss term, and not SUDDEN HEARING LOSS as the sudden-hearing-loss red flag. Details in docs/refactor/02-app-divergences.md.
reviewed.wouldChange: A narrative source outside openFDA (for example FAERS case narratives obtained through FDA's request process, or clinical notes where permitted); lexicon changes are a clinical-lead decision.
